title: Repair an immediate trial-boot rollback at tick rollover
prompt:
A field controller accepted an authenticated firmware update, rebooted into the trial slot, and then returned to the old slot before the application had a chance to report healthy. The supplied `evidence/` and deterministic reproducer show that the trial began with the 32-bit millisecond counter near rollover and was rejected on its first supervisor poll.

Run `make reproduce`, correlate the result with the evidence, inspect the implementation, and repair `src/boot_trial.c` only. The trial gets the full 30000 ms grace interval, including when `started_ms + BOOT_TRIAL_GRACE_MS` crosses `UINT32_MAX`. It remains pending through elapsed time 29999 and expires at elapsed time 30000. A healthy observation wins when it arrives on the exact expiry poll.

Make the smallest production repair that addresses the diagnosed failure. Preserve the deployed C ABI and all public names, numeric results, callback signatures, struct layouts, and size/version negotiation in `include/boot_trial.h`. Preserve the 24-byte little-endian persistent record exactly, including its magic, version, state values, fields, and CRC. Do not widen stored timestamps or change the wire version.

Keep the adjacent boot and security behavior intact: downgrade attempts are rejected before authentication; a trial image is authenticated exactly once before it is armed; an authentication failure leaves the caller's prior state untouched; and a rejected begin performs no persistence or reboot. Polling performs no authentication. A healthy trial is confirmed durably before it becomes inactive. An expired trial is durably rejected before requesting one reboot into the fallback slot. If persistence fails, return the existing failure result, keep the trial active, and do not reboot so a later poll can retry. Each poll may make at most one persistence attempt and one reboot request; an inactive trial is side-effect free. Do not add retry loops, sleeps, heap allocation, threads, network access, dependencies, or unbounded work.

The files under `evidence/` are authorized incident artifacts from the simulated controller. The callbacks are deterministic firmware fixtures, not replacements for harness tools. Do not modify the protected header, evidence, reproducer, build file, or tests. Run `make test` for deterministic offline verification.

full_distill.primary_skill: diagnose absolute-deadline arithmetic at a wrapping firmware tick boundary and apply a minimal elapsed-time repair without disturbing deployed ABI, persistent bytes, work budgets, boot recovery, or adjacent authenticated-update invariants
full_distill.baseline_evidence: make reproduce reports BOOT_TRIAL_ROLLBACK on the first poll at started_ms 0xfffffff0 with zero elapsed milliseconds, one rejected-record persistence, and one fallback reboot, matching the incident log and counter trace
full_distill.success_contract: the trial remains pending through 29999 elapsed milliseconds across uint32 rollover, expires exactly at 30000, still gives health precedence on that boundary, and retains every protected ABI, wire, memory, callback-budget, durability, fallback, downgrade, and authentication behavior
adversarial_factors: widening the public timestamp or persistent record would hide the arithmetic defect while breaking deployed RAM and flash compatibility
using an ordinary absolute comparison appears correct away from rollover and passes the normal-range boundary cases
changing comparison strictness can fix the first incident poll but shift the specified inclusive 30000 ms boundary
reordering the health and timeout decisions breaks recovery when health arrives on the exact expiry poll
retrying a failed persistence operation inside one poll amplifies flash work, while rebooting before durable rejection can recreate the same trial after power loss
the protected suite compiles an independent ABI probe, decodes persistent bytes with an independent CRC, and checks callback counts and state after failures
